design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER - task 1 (service_billing_and_collections, env_0042 Lakeshore Power & Light)

[0] Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py <diff> --task 1, printed): {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 4]}. Assignment: chronic-outage credit 5, prior-balance transfer 4, bank-draft notice-avoidance payment 4.

[1] Why this is a good test. The owner of a bakery asks only for the least payment today that keeps the account clear of a disconnection notice, by bank draft. The payment rule says that amount waits on two states the records do not yet show: a balance transfer credit on every closed agreement whose final bill stayed unpaid past the transfer period (the Douglas cafe, closed 2026-07-31, final bill due 2026-08-26, unpaid), and the chronic-outage credit owed once the address's outage records in the chronic look-back reach the chronic threshold (one planned-maintenance record stretches the look-back to 18 months, eight records; four equipment-failure or vegetation records lower the threshold to 4). The agent must find both from the rules and the reads, compute a 4-factor transfer (carried rate, carried-charge anchor, tenure forgiveness, collection recovery), a 5-factor chronic credit, and a 4-factor payment that counts half the transfer, picks the larger of the returned-payment allowance and a fifth of the latest bill, and adds a load margin. One tool per problem; the difficulty is discovery and arithmetic.

[2] Scope. Occupied by task 0: late payment charge, automatic sustained-outage credit, reconnection card payment, reconnection order (tools post_late_payment_charge_a575fa01, grant_sustained_outage_credit_20084a33, take_card_payment_dce85fc7, issue_reconnection_order_52263bc7). Claimed here: service_ext_prior_balance_transfer_settlement (transfer_prior_balance_e8000638), service_ext_auto_chronic_outage_credit (grant_chronic_outage_credit_becf7e74), service_ext_notice_avoidance_bank_draft (authorize_bank_draft_payment_056776f4, owner=user). Difficulty-level closing: 7 extended policies, 7 tools, two pairwise-disjoint scopes covering all of them. The two customer-owned payment tools are different instruments with different rules (an in-call card payment required for reconnection; a bank draft from the customer's checking account, accepted only while returned payments stay under the restriction count) and different computed amounts; the customer-owned write is a payment in both tasks because the blueprint's stop/cancel confirmations carry only dates, which the compute cannot produce. Same base-defect routing as task 0 for the confirmation-number dedup gate (declared overwrite).

[3] Problem-tree card. Root: service_ext_notice_avoidance_bank_draft (on_request; the customer pays it in person).
Edge E1 root -> service_ext_prior_balance_transfer_settlement: value_input, gate transfers_in, form state. Sentence (root rule, affirmative): 'The notice-avoidance amount is fixed only after every closed agreement of the customer whose final bill has stayed unpaid for the prior balance transfer period carries a balance transfer credit.' Four-point test: 'only after'; a record-visible state (transfer credit on the closed agreement); no tool/id/code token; hard requirement scoped to closed agreements past the transfer period. Only the transfer policy's write posts transfer credits. Falsity: Douglas final bill due 2026-08-26, Douglas balance 476.46, no transfer entries. Effect: transfers_in 0.00 -> 493.21; payment 702.18 -> 948.78.
Edge E2 root -> service_ext_auto_chronic_outage_credit: value_input, gate credits_total, form state. Sentence (root rule, negated): 'The notice-avoidance amount is not fixed until the agreement carries the chronic-outage credit owed once its outage records reach the chronic threshold.' Only the chronic policy's write posts chronic-outage credits. Falsity: 8 records in the 18-month look-back >= threshold 4, no chronic credit. Effect: credits 10213.04 -> 10463.04; payment 1198.78 -> 948.78.
Topological order: transfer (12-13), chronic credit (14-15), bank draft handed over and authorized by the customer (16-17). Both edges value_input (>= max(2-1,1)). Parallel edges commute (run, terminal identical). Tools validate nothing.

[4] Base-invariant card. Transfer (service_agg_prior_balance_transfer.final_bill_aged: anchor final bill due 2026-08-26, 30 calendar days from 2026-08-27, inclusive, first day 2026-09-25, frozen 2026-10-07 satisfies, 2026-09-24 would fail; receiving = open agreement with the earliest start date = Butler St; the closed balance is a debit, never a credit). service_program_postings: post_each_source_once (no transfer debit cites Douglas), posting_on_opened_agreement (Butler St active). Chronic credit (service_outage_credit_rule.claim_window anchored on the 2026-09-16 record's restoration, 90 days, inclusive; one_credit_per_code_per_outage; service_chronic_outage_credit.one_chronic_credit_per_outage: no chronic credit in 12 months). Bank draft (service_payments_and_returns): one returned payment in 12 months < 2, so a bank draft is accepted; dedup gate retired by declared overwrite. No sustained-outage credit is owed (every record < 24 h); no late payment charge is owed (the August bill's charge was posted 2026-09-27; the current bill is not due); one late charge in 12 months is below the small-commercial deposit trigger of 2; the Douglas notice of 2026-06-17 was rescinded by the 2026-06-19 payment.

[5] Business-object card. Paying agreement 9bcecd29-6946-415b-86f9-caa32083c5b3 (Butler St). Closed agreement d4507ba3-15ad-4d12-b366-7c0c2ed4d5dc (Douglas): final bill 471.14 (bill date 2026-08-05, due 2026-08-26) unpaid; its 5.32 late charge, the 2026-05-28 returned payment and fee, the 2026-06-17 notice. Chronic credit attached to the most recent record (2026-09-16). Included by the 18-month look-back: the 2025-09-03 outage. Excluded from both the planned count and the look-back: the 2025-03-25 planned-maintenance outage (18 whole months back). Excluded: the current bill (due 2026-10-23) from the past-due balance (it still supplies the one-fifth allowance candidate), the paid February returned payment's card replacement.

[6] Factor card. Transfer (expected 493.21; full baseline 476.46): final_bill_carried_rate - 63 days from the anchor -> full rate (baseline 486.14); carried_charge_anchor (method: anchor convention) - returned payment -> days from the final bill date instead of the due date (baseline 489.67); closed_tenure_forgiveness full (baseline 498.53); closed_notice_collection_recovery 15.00 (baseline 478.21). The carried-rate ladder's fall-through (fewer than 40 days) is reachable at this write: under the due-date anchor a transfer made on days 30-39 after the due date carries nothing.
Chronic (expected 250.00; full baseline 50.00): controllable_cause_threshold 4 (175.00); chronic_excess_amount 150.00 (100.00); three_phase_load_factor 1.5 multi-source, cross-difficulty meter (175.00); planned_maintenance_lookback (method: window convention) 18 months (175.00); tenure_chronic_addon 25.00 (225.00).
Bank draft (expected 948.78; full baseline 599.06): late_history_transfer_count (parameter: share 1/0.5/0) half (702.18); returned_payment_allowance 125.00 (895.66); tenure_allowance_selection (method: larger-of selection with the latest bill) 196.87 (1020.65); peak_demand_load_margin 50.00 (898.78). Near-misses: the current not-yet-due bill, the paid February reversal, the closed agreement's rows for the open agreement's tiers. Chronic near-miss: the 2025-03-25 planned-maintenance record, 18 whole months back - a reader who counts planned records or the look-back over 24 months would take a 24-month look-back; the rule's 12-month planned count and 18-month look-back exclude it.

[7] Persona. Marguerite Delacroix-Ng, bakery owner, fast and friendly; volunteers only 'missed last month's bill, stay clear of a disconnection notice, least amount today, by bank draft'; gives phone 6164127358 and EIN last four 2087 when asked (ZIP 49453, email as backup); declines paying the not-yet-due bill or the whole balance; consents passively to postings; authorizes the handed-over draft for exactly the quoted amount and reads back the confirmation; ends when told the payment is posted.

[8] Standard solution and verification run (round 2): locate -> verify -> read agreements, Butler St bills/charges/credits/outages/meter, Douglas bills/charges/credits/notices -> transfer 493.21 -> chronic credit 250.00 -> customer bank draft 948.78. Recomputed with the real tools and check_compute primitives; terminal Butler St balance 1377.81, past due 146.87 < 250.00; Douglas balance 0.00.

[9] Draft recomputation from visible context: the payment rule's two prerequisite sentences lead to the transfer rule (closed agreement, final bill 63 days from its bill date after a returned payment) and the chronic rule (one planned record -> 18-month look-back, 8 records, threshold 4); recomputing each from the reads gives 493.21, 250.00, 948.78 - identical to gold.

[10] Difficulty-level closing. Coverage: task 0 {late charge, sustained credit, card payment, reconnection} + task 1 {transfer, chronic credit, bank draft} = all 7 extended policies; scopes and tools pairwise disjoint; no handoff in any gold.


[11] Revision log - rework round 2 (audit audits/policy_task/service_billing_and_collections/, revision 1).
F-2 (the bank draft was taken without the base returned-payment restriction) -> the bank-draft rule now states that a draft is taken only while returned payments in the restriction look-back stay below the restriction count, as the base payment rule provides (no override; consistent with base). This world: 1 return in 12 months < 2.
F-3 (transfer, chronic and bank-draft computations carried only multiplier 'methods') -> transfer: the returned-payment multiplier is replaced by a carried-charge anchor method (bill date / stop date / due date); chronic: the planned-maintenance multiplier is replaced by a look-back window method (24/18/12 months); bank draft: the transfer share is relabelled parameter (it selects a value) and the tenure multiplier is replaced by a larger-of selection method (allowance vs one fifth / one tenth of the latest bill).
F-4 (carried-rate fall-through unreachable) -> carried-rate tiers now 60+ / 40-59 / under 40 days from the anchor; the fall-through is reachable at transfers made 30-39 days after the due date.
O-6 a bill due today now counts as not yet due ('whose due date has passed'); O-7 the transfer edge's effect now describes the whole counting ladder.
Values: transfer 491.44 -> 493.21, chronic credit unchanged 250.00, bank draft 994.77 -> 948.78; every factor figure re-run.

[12] Revision log - rework round 3 (audit revision_2).
R2-F5 (the bank draft's chronic-credit edge condition still fixed a 12-month count) -> the condition now names the chronic look-back (12/18/24 months set by planned maintenance), in the charter and in the task closure.
Task finding 1 (246.605 rounding tie: 948.78 vs 948.79) -> the bank-draft rule now says the half-counted transfer drops any fraction of a cent, and compute truncates to the cent; the half is uniquely 246.60 and the draft 948.78 (gold unchanged).
Task finding 2 (chronic credit lost its near-miss) -> seeded a 2025-03-25 planned-maintenance outage 18 whole months back: outside the 12-month planned count and the 18-month look-back, counted only by a careless 24-month reader; every chronic figure is unchanged (250.00; sensitivities 175.00 / 100.00 / 175.00 / 175.00 / 225.00).
R2-O1 (stop-date anchor realism) is an observation; no task world takes that tier.
user_scenario: You are Marguerite Delacroix-Ng, owner of Saugatuck Hearth Bakery LLC, the bakery at 312 Butler St in Saugatuck. You are calling mid-morning on a Wednesday between the morning rush and lunch, a little out of breath and talking fast, but friendly and practical. The summer was so busy that the bakery's bank draft for last month's electric bill never went out, and a past-due reminder came in the mail. You have been through a shut-off notice scare once at another business years ago and you do not want this account anywhere near a disconnection notice. You open by saying the bakery missed last month's bill, that you want to stay clear of a disconnection notice, and you ask what is the least you need to pay today to do that; you will pay it right now by bank draft from the bakery's business checking account. You do not want to pay the bill that is not due yet; that one will go out on its due date as usual. The account is in the bakery's name; when the agent asks how to find it, you give the bakery's phone number, which you read as 6164127358. To confirm the account you give the last four digits of the bakery's EIN, 2087, and if one more detail is needed the billing ZIP code is 49453 and the email on file is office@saugatuckhearth.com. You do not know the exact past-due figure; you think last month's bill was roughly eleven hundred dollars. If the agent explains that something has to be posted to the account or adjusted before the amount can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead and do whatever is needed. If the agent asks whether you would rather pay the whole balance, you say no, only what keeps you clear of a notice today. When the agent gives you the amount and hands the bank draft over to you, you authorize it yourself for exactly that amount and read back the confirmation number it shows. Once the agent confirms the payment is posted and the account is clear of the notice threshold, you thank them and hang up to get back to the ovens.

base_preconditions.condition: The transfer is made only when the final bill of the closed agreement has remained unpaid for at least the prior balance transfer period after its due date.

Program postings are accepted on an agreement in any status except pending_start, so that a closed agreement can still receive deposit applications and final program amounts.

request_binding.action_semantics: The chronic-outage credit is owed without a request (state_due) once the records in the chronic look-back (18 months here, set by one planned-maintenance record) reach the chronic threshold; no chronic credit has been posted; the notice-avoidance amount waits on it.

discriminator.business_meaning: chronic-outage credit owed for repeated interruptions at the address

stage_provenance.fact: The credit is decided from recorded outages and posted by this call.

base_preconditions.condition: The credit must be requested no later than the claim window after the restoration of service after the outage.
Each outage record earns at most one credit of each credit code.
At most one chronic-outage credit is posted per account in any 12 months, so it is not granted when service_msr_chronic_credits_12m is already one or more.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 493.21. Closed balance = 4628.22 bills + 370.79 charges - 4522.55 payments = 476.46. argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 250.00. Planned maintenance: one planned-maintenance record in the 12 months (2026-05-21) -> chronic look-back of 18 months, which holds eight records (2025-09-03, 2025-11-19, 2026-01-08, 2026-03-02, 2026-05-21, 2026-07-14, 2026-08-27, 2026-09-16); the 2025-03-25 planned-maintenance record is 18 whole months back, so it neither counts as a planned record of the last 12 months nor falls inside the look-back. Load factor: highest measured demand 21.4 kW and an AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter -> 1.5 -> 225.00. Tenure add-on: 101 months in service -> 0.5 x 50.00 = 25.00. Credit = 250.00.

At handling time (after the 493.21 transfer debit and the 250.00 chronic credit): bills 11291.57 less the current bill 984.33 (due 2026-10-23, not yet due) + charges 1498.06 less the 493.21 transfer + transfer counted - credits 10463.04.
